title: Signal garden — self-review scratchbook
content:
Purpose / framing:
This is a working scratchbook for my quarterly self-review and manager prep. Not a polished narrative — a place to collect small signals, quick evidence, and top-of-mind asks I want to surface in a 1:1 or calibration. Triage: highlight 2–3 outcomes, bring 3 supporting signals each, and capture 2 calibration questions and 2 asks.

Context / role focus:
- Role: Senior People Operations Partner (embedded with Growth & Platform eng teams).
- Goal this quarter: reduce time-to-onboard for mid-senior engineers, unblock hiring coordination for Dedicated product, and lift cross-team incident postmortem hygiene. 
- Why these matter: onboarding + hiring cadence directly impacts time-to-value for new infra hires; PMs flagged repeated handoffs on Dedicated capacity features; SRE/Serving-runtime teams want clearer postmortem artifacts to accelerate RCA.

Top 3 outcomes I want to claim (working):
1) Cut average onboarding time (first 6 weeks to independent contributor) for infra/eng by 15% via a staged checklist + buddy program.
2) Reduce time-to-offer for Dedicated hiring pipeline by 20% through synchronous interview scheduling and a hiring coordinator template.
3) Improve postmortem completeness score (rough internal rubric) from ~60% → 85% for sev-2s by running a short playbook and office-hours for PM/eng leads.

Signals / evidence (raw, keep it short):
Outcome 1 — onboarding speed: 
- Pilot cohort (n=6) started Jan 12; avg independent contributor date: 32 days (target baseline 38) — interim signal: ~16% improvement.
- Buddy survey (n=5): 4/5 felt checklist reduced confusion on infra ownership; common friction: VPN and private model access steps still unclear.
- Quick metric: mean number of Slack pings to eng-oncall in week 1 down from 14 → 9 in pilot.

Outcome 2 — hiring throughput: 
- Time-to-offer for Dedicated eng reqs (2 reqs) went from 42 → 34 days after introducing synchronized interview blocks and a 2-hour coordinator window.
- Blocker: Hiring manager availability and unclear scorecard alignment caused 3-day stall on one req (noted in PEO-4123).
- Signal: Candidate NPS (post-offer feedback) improved; one candidate commented positively about clear timeline.

Outcome 3 — postmortem hygiene:
- Ran 3 office-hours + shared one-pager playbook; two sev-2s in Feb had PM/eng co-authored postmortems vs prior single-author artifacts.
- Postmortem checklist adoption: 6 teams adopted template (loose adoption, needs enforcement).
- Anecdote: infra lead said playbook clarified alert routing ownership and saved a follow-up meeting.

Quick wins to highlight in sync:
- Pilot onboarding checklist reduced early Slack noise (quantify: -5 pings/week per person).
- Coordinated interview blocks cut recruiter coordination time ~30m per req.
- One-pager postmortem playbook received positive Slack thread from SRE manager.

Manager prep bullets (what I will say, short):
- I ran three small experiments this quarter (onboarding checklist + buddy, synchronized interview blocks, postmortem playbook). Early signs show traction; need support to scale.
- Ask: 0.2 Ops FTE for 2 months to operationalize hiring coordinator template and run next onboarding cohort measurement.
- Ask: brief mandate in Eng Leadership weekly to require PM+Eng co-authorship on sev-2 postmortems for the next quarter (lightweight enforcement).
- Calibration question: is the org comfortable trading a small lift (0.2 FTE) for faster hiring velocity that accelerates two product release timelines?

Potential risks / blockers I want to flag:
- Dependency: Dedicated hiring success depends on scorecard alignment and hiring manager calendar availability — need Manager buy-in.
- Resource: Ops bandwidth is thin in March (conflicting project: benefits open-enrollment). If we don’t get a short-term FTE, scale will stall.
- Cultural: Some teams resist templated postmortems — will need leadership example + peer review to normalize.

Draft ask language (two variants):
1) Concise: "Requesting 0.2 Ops FTE for two months to finalize and roll out hiring coordinator playbook and measure TTO impact."
2) Narrative: "We piloted three operational experiments that together shave ~1–2 weeks off onboarding/hiring friction for infra and Dedicated teams. To turn signals into consistent outcomes we need a focused Ops headroom (~0.2 FTE, two months) to run the playbook, train hiring managers, and own measurement. This investment should accelerate two near-term hires that are on the critical path for Q2 launches."

Calibration questions I want to ask manager / during calibration:
- Where do we prioritize: speed-to-hire (shorter time-to-offer) vs richer candidate evaluation (longer loops)?
- Is a temporary 0.2 Ops FTE a reasonable trade for improved hiring velocity and better postmortem hygiene?
- If leadership prefers not to fund FTE, would manager-level participation in a 3-week focused "hiring blitz" be acceptable?

Next actions (me as owner):
- Draft short one-pager for the 1:1 with the asks and attach pilot metrics (Due: Mar 11).
- Share onboarding checklist + anonymized buddy survey results with Eng leads (Due: Mar 12).
- Run a 30-min sync with Recruiters + Hiring Managers to lock 2-week calendar windows for Dedicated reqs (Due: Mar 16).

Loose threads / notes to self:
- VPN + private model access steps: create a 1-click guide or pre-provision request form.
- Add a tiny tracking column to the onboarding checklist: "blocked_by" with owner to reduce unknowns.
- Consider a lightweight PM+Eng postmortem rubric (3 questions) to speed reviews.
- Connect with Mira to see if benefits open-enrollment schedule can shift to free up Ops capacity in mid-March.

Anything to brag about (keep short):
- Pilot cohort metrics look encouraging; avoid overstating — small n, but directionally positive.

Notes to self for final self-review narrative:
- Frame as experiments → signals → scale ask. Use three clean charts: onboarding days, time-to-offer, postmortem completeness. Keep examples crisp.
- Bring one short anecdote from a new hire "first week" to humanize the impact.
